subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which political party was founded by Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee in October 1951?
questions.explanation: Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee founded the Bharatiya Jana Sangh in October 1951, which emphasized the ideology of 'One country, one culture, one nation'.

questions.question: The Swatantra Party was founded in 1959 under the leadership of which prominent Indian statesman?
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari ('Rajaji') founded the Swatantra Party in August 1959 to advocate free enterprise and oppose state-led socialist planning.

questions.question: What was the name of the brutal paramilitary force organized by Kasim Razvi in the princely state of Hyderabad to oppose integration with India?
questions.explanation: The Razakars were an extremist sectarian paramilitary wing in Hyderabad that unleashed violence and atrocities against citizens protesting the Nizam's rule.

questions.question: What was the code name of the Indian Army military operation launched in September 1948 to integrate the princely state of Hyderabad?
questions.explanation: Operation Polo was the police action launched by the Indian armed forces in September 1948 which led to the surrender of the Nizam of Hyderabad.

questions.question: In which year did the bilingual Bombay state get divided into the separate unilingual linguistic states of Maharashtra and Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Following intense agitation by Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti and Mahagujarat Andolan, Bombay state was bifurcated into Maharashtra and Gujarat on 1 May 1960.

questions.question: In 1944, a group of leading industrial tycoons met in Bombay and drafted a joint proposal for economic development popularly known as the:
questions.explanation: The Bombay Plan was drawn up in 1944 by prominent industrialists like J.R.D. Tata and G.D. Birla, advocating strong state initiative in heavy industry and infrastructure.

questions.question: The National Development Council (NDC) of India was established in which year to associate the states with the planning process?
questions.explanation: The National Development Council was set up in August 1952, presided over by the Prime Minister and comprising all Union Cabinet ministers and Chief Ministers of all states.

questions.question: Which agricultural scientist is widely revered as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'?
questions.explanation: Dr. M.S. Swaminathan led the introduction of High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds of wheat and rice along with chemical fertilizers, initiating the Green Revolution in India.

questions.question: Which spiritual and political leader of Tibet sought political asylum in India in 1959 after the Chinese suppression of the Tibetan uprising?
questions.explanation: The 14th Dalai Lama fled Lhasa and was granted political asylum in India by Jawaharlal Nehru in March 1959, which angered the Chinese government.

questions.question: Which historic bilateral treaty was signed between India and Pakistan in July 1972 by Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto following the 1971 war?
questions.explanation: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972, committing India and Pakistan to resolve all bilateral disputes peacefully through bilateral negotiations.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Who was the Congress President from Tamil Nadu who proposed that senior party leaders should resign from government ministries to work for party organisation?
questions.explanation: K. Kamaraj proposed the famous 'Kamaraj Plan' in 1963, urging senior ministers to step down from government posts to devote full time to grassroots organizational work.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: The famous political expression 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram' originated after frequent party-switching by an MLA in which Indian state in 1967?
questions.explanation: The phrase originated when Gaya Lal, an MLA in Haryana, changed his party allegiance thrice in a fortnight in 1967, giving birth to the catchphrase 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram'.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act officially abolished the Privy Purses and royal privileges of the former princely rulers in 1971?
questions.explanation: The 26th Constitutional Amendment Act passed in 1971 officially terminated the Privy Purses and recognized titles of former rulers of princely states.

questions.question: In January 1974, engineering college students in Gujarat started a mass agitation against price rise and corruption called the:
questions.explanation: The Navnirman Movement began in Gujarat in January 1974 against rising foodgrain prices, leading to the dissolution of the state assembly and fresh elections.

questions.question: Under whose leadership was the historic nationwide 20-day Railway Strike organized in May 1974?
questions.explanation: George Fernandes led the National Coordination Committee for Railwaymen's Struggle (NCCRS) in May 1974, bringing India's rail network to a halt.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution was the National Emergency proclaimed in June 1975 on grounds of 'internal disturbance'?
questions.explanation: The Emergency was declared on 25 June 1975 under Article 352, which empowered the President to proclaim an emergency if India's security was threatened by war or internal disturbance.

questions.question: Which military operation was carried out by the Indian Army inside the Golden Temple complex at Amritsar in June 1984?
questions.explanation: Operation Blue Star was conducted between 1 and 8 June 1984 to flush out armed Sikh militants holed up inside the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar.

questions.question: Who was the leader of the Mizo National Front (MNF) who led an armed secessionist movement for two decades before signing the 1986 peace accord?
questions.explanation: Laldenga formed the Mizo National Front in 1961 and led an armed insurgency from 1966 until signing the historic Mizo Accord with Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in 1986.

questions.question: Which Prime Minister headed the National Front coalition government that implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations in August 1990?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Vishwanath Pratap Singh announced the decision to implement the Mandal Commission's recommendation of 27% OBC reservation in central government jobs on 7 August 1990.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Who became the first popularly elected President of the Russian Federation following the collapse of the Soviet Union?
questions.explanation: Boris Yeltsin emerged as the hero of the resistance against the August 1991 coup and served as the first President of the Russian Federation from 1991 to 1999.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which Central Asian post-Soviet republic witnessed a devastating civil war that lasted for ten years, ending in 2002?
questions.explanation: Tajikistan was engulfed in a severe sectarian and regional civil war from 1992 to 1997 with residual clashes continuing until 2002.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: In which year was the common European currency, the Euro, officially introduced as physical banknotes and coins?
questions.explanation: While adopted for accounting and electronic transfers in 1999, physical Euro coins and currency notes entered public circulation in 12 EU member states on 1 January 2002.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which Chinese leader declared the landmark 'Open Door Policy' and modern economic reforms in December 1978?
questions.explanation: Deng Xiaoping announced the 'Open Door Policy' at the third plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978, initiating China's market-oriented reforms.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Article 9 of the constitution of which Asian nation renounces war as a sovereign right and pledges never to maintain land, sea, or air forces?
questions.explanation: Article 9 of Japan's 1947 post-war 'Peace Constitution' explicitly renounces war as an instrument of state policy and forbids the maintenance of offensive armed forces.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which military general ousted Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in a bloodless military coup in Pakistan in October 1999?
questions.explanation: Army Chief General Pervez Musharraf staged a military coup on 12 October 1999, removing Nawaz Sharif and ruling Pakistan until 2008.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In which year did the constitutional monarchy end and Nepal officially transform into a Federal Democratic Republic?
questions.explanation: The newly elected Constituent Assembly of Nepal voted overwhelmingly to abolish the 240-year-old monarchy on 28 May 2008, declaring Nepal a federal republic.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which autonomous UN agency was established in 1957 following US President Eisenhower's 'Atoms for Peace' proposal to promote safe nuclear technology?
questions.explanation: The IAEA was created in Vienna in 1957 as an autonomous organisation to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy and prevent its diversion to military purposes.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which international human rights NGO was founded in 1961 by British lawyer Peter Benenson to campaign for prisoners of conscience?
questions.explanation: Amnesty International was established in London in 1961 by Peter Benenson to campaign against abuses of human rights and defend prisoners of conscience globally.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: The historic 1987 Montreal Protocol was negotiated by the international community to protect which vital environmental component?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer was adopted in September 1987 to phase out the production of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).

questions.question: The term 'McDonaldisation' in cultural debates on globalisation is primarily associated with which process?
questions.explanation: McDonaldisation describes cultural homogenisation, where consumer cultural habits, fast-food norms, and lifestyles of powerful Western nations spread globally.

questions.question: The Congress Party's ability to accommodate diverse social, regional, and ideological groups in the first two decades led political scientist Rajni Kothari to describe it as a:
options: C) Coalition of diverse interests and factions within a dominant party framework
D) Regional alliance of provincial satraps with no central command
questions.explanation: Rajni Kothari conceptualized the 'Congress System' as a grand umbrella coalition containing diverse social groups, ideologies, and competitive internal factions.

questions.question: The three-member States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) constituted in 1953 comprised Justice Fazal Ali as Chairman along with which other two distinguished members?
options: A) Pattabhi Sitaramayya and K.M. Munshi
B) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer
C) G.B. Pant and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
D) K.M. Panikkar and Hriday Nath Kunzru
questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Commission (1953) consisted of Justice Fazal Ali (Chairman), historian K.M. Panikkar, and parliamentarian Pandit Hriday Nath Kunzru.

questions.question: Why did the Government of India declare three consecutive 'Annual Plans' (Plan Holidays) between 1966 and 1969 instead of launching the Fourth Five Year Plan immediately?
options: A) Due to severe economic crises caused by the 1965 war, successive droughts, and devaluation of the rupee
B) Due to the nationwide suspension of industrial production under the Emergency
C) Due to a complete embargo on foreign technology imports by the United Nations
D) Due to the abolition of the Planning Commission by the Janata Party government
questions.explanation: Consecutive wars with China (1962) and Pakistan (1965), consecutive monsoon failures in 1965-66 causing famine, and rupee devaluation led to 'Plan Holidays' from 1966 to 1969.

questions.question: In August 1971, amidst escalating tensions in East Pakistan, India signed the 20-year Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation with which major superpower?
options: A) The United States of America
C) The People's Republic of China
questions.explanation: On 9 August 1971, Foreign Minister Swaran Singh and Soviet Foreign Minister Andrei Gromyko signed the 20-year Treaty to deter potential American-Chinese intervention during the Bangladesh crisis.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the fourth General Election of 1967, coalition governments comprising diverse non-Congress opposition parties were formed in multiple states under which collective label?
questions.explanation: The 1967 elections produced non-Congress coalition governments in eight states called Samyukta Vidhayak Dal (SVD) governments, uniting disparate parties like SSP, PSP, BJS, and BKD.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which group of veteran Congress organizational leaders who controlled the party apparatus during Indira Gandhi's early tenure was informally known as the:
questions.explanation: The 'Syndicate' was the informal name for a powerful group of senior Congress leaders including K. Kamaraj, S.K. Patil, N. Sanjiva Reddy, and Atulya Ghosh who held sway over the party organization.

questions.question: Which controversial constitutional amendment passed in 1976 during the Emergency introduced sweeping changes, earning it the label of a 'mini-Constitution'?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 altered the Preamble (adding 'Secular', 'Socialist', 'Integrity'), curtailed fundamental rights, extended parliamentary tenure to 6 years, and curtailed judicial review.

questions.question: Following the 1977 election defeat of the Congress, which prominent leader merged his newly formed 'Congress for Democracy' party into the Janata Party?
questions.explanation: Senior Dalit leader Jagjivan Ram resigned from Indira Gandhi's cabinet along with H.N. Bahuguna in February 1977, launched 'Congress for Democracy' (CFD), and soon merged it into the Janata Party.

questions.question: The historic Punjab Accord of July 1985 aimed at restoring peace in Punjab was signed between Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and which Akali Dal leader?
questions.explanation: The Rajiv-Longowal Accord (Punjab Accord) was signed on 24 July 1985 between Rajiv Gandhi and Akali Dal President Sant Harchand Singh Longowal.

questions.question: The Kanshi Ram-led organisation BAMCEF, established in 1978, stands for:
options: A) Backward and Marginalised Castes Economic Front
B) Bahujan Association of Minorities and Cultural Employees Federation
C) Backward Areas Mining and Construction Employees Federation
D) Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation
questions.explanation: Kanshi Ram founded BAMCEF in 1978 as a non-political, non-electoral federation of educated employees from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, and religious minorities.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which of the following was a direct economic consequence of 'Shock Therapy' in Russia during the early 1990s?
options: A) The dramatic devaluation of the ruble and inflation wiping out citizens' bank savings
B) The complete eradication of income inequality across Russian society
C) The massive increase in the state-funded social welfare subsidies
D) The elimination of private monopolies and rapid rise in public healthcare spending
questions.explanation: Shock Therapy caused a 90% plunge in state industrial assets ('the largest garage sale in history'), runaway hyperinflation, ruble devaluation, and devastation of citizens' life savings.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the primary function of the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF), established in 1994?
options: A) To maintain a standing collective military rapid reaction force for ASEAN
B) To facilitate multilateral dialogue and consultations on political and security cooperation in the Asia-Pacific
C) To regulate foreign exchange rates and monetary reserves across Southeast Asia
D) To formulate binding international copyright treaties for Asian electronics manufacturers
questions.explanation: Established in 1994, the ARF provides a premier multilateral consultative forum to foster constructive dialogue and consultation on political and security issues among 27 member states.

questions.question: In international security studies, the 'traditional' concept of security primarily emphasizes:
options: A) Eradication of global poverty, infectious diseases, and illiteracy
B) Protection of human rights and ecological conservation of the global commons
C) Protection of state sovereignty, territorial integrity, and military defense against external aggression
D) Universal basic income and digital data protection for global citizens
questions.explanation: Traditional security focuses on national security against military threats from other states, emphasizing deterrence, defense, balance of power, and alliance building.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: The 1987 Brundtland Commission Report, which popularized the paradigm of 'Sustainable Development', was officially titled:
questions.explanation: The World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED), headed by Gro Harlem Brundtland, released the landmark report 'Our Common Future' in 1987.

questions.question: Where did the fourth annual gathering of the World Social Forum (WSF) take place in January 2004, marking its first session held outside Brazil?
questions.explanation: The WSF met outside Brazil for the first time in January 2004 in Mumbai, India, bringing together over 100,000 delegates from grassroots global civil society movements.

questions.question: Which of the following commissions/committees appointed by the Constituent Assembly in 1948 specifically recommended that Indian states should NOT be reorganised purely on a linguistic basis at that juncture?
questions.explanation: The Linguistic Provinces Commission headed by Justice S.K. Dhar (appointed in June 1948) recommended that the reorganisation of states should be based on administrative convenience rather than exclusively on linguistic criteria.

questions.question: During the 1962 Sino-Indian War, who was India's Defense Minister who faced severe domestic criticism for the military debacle and subsequently resigned from Nehru's cabinet?
questions.explanation: V.K. Krishna Menon resigned as Defense Minister in November 1962 in the wake of the Chinese border offensive and parliamentary outrage over India's lack of military preparedness.

questions.question: In the famous habeas corpus case during the Emergency (ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla, April 1976), which lone Supreme Court judge delivered a courageous dissenting verdict asserting that the right to life cannot be suspended even during an emergency?
questions.explanation: Justice H.R. Khanna delivered the sole dissenting opinion in the ADM Jabalpur ruling, upholding personal liberty; he was subsequently superseded for the office of Chief Justice of India by Justice M.H. Beg in 1977.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which post-communist country in the Balkans underwent a violent, bloody disintegration in the 1990s, splitting into multiple sovereign republics including Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbia, and Montenegro?
questions.explanation: The Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia collapsed into inter-ethnic civil warfare during the 1990s, fracturing into Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Macedonia, and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro).

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which international environmental treaty was adopted in 1959 to demilitarize and designate an entire continent exclusively for peaceful scientific research and free from territorial claims?
questions.explanation: Signed in Washington in December 1959, the Antarctic Treaty froze sovereign territorial claims, banned military bases, weapons testing, and nuclear waste disposal, dedicating Antarctica to peaceful scientific investigation.
